chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who said to another: 'Sell me the fruit of your palm tree, this one in it, for two qafizs of dates, or less or more, specifying whatever he wishes,' and he sold it: 'There is no objection to it.' He also said: 'Dates and unripe dates (busr) from a single palm tree are permissible (in sale), but if old dates and unripe dates are mixed, it is not valid, and raisins and grapes are the same.'

key_terms.ثَمَرَة: fruit (specifically the produce of a tree)
key_terms.قَفِيزَانِ: two qafizs (a unit of volume measurement)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for the validity of selling fruit from palm trees in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that selling unripe fruit (thamar) for a specified amount of dates is permissible even if the exact quantity varies, provided the type is agreed upon. However, he prohibits mixing old dates (tamr) with unripe dates (busr) or raisins with grapes in the same transaction due to uncertainty (gharar) in quality and quantity, a principle derived from the Prophet's prohibition of 'sale of what is in the belly' (bay' al-ma'iq). This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on minimizing ambiguity in commercial contracts to ensure fairness and prevent dispute.
